before.title: THE SPOON’S NEW OFFICE
before.text: You discover that dropping a spoon makes {{carer}} fetch it. The office has no salary, but excellent powers.

choices.label: Drop it a second time

outcome.text: {{carer}} retrieves it, then moves the bowl beyond your jurisdiction.

choices.label: Offer the spoon back

outcome.text: {{carer}} accepts the damp gift with ceremony. You have invented an inefficient but pleasant form of cooperation.

after.title: THE SPOON GOES DOWN AGAIN
after.text: You drop your spoon. {{carer.intro}} picks it up. By the fifth time, the smile has gone and the spoon is being held very firmly.

choices.label: Drop it once more

outcome.text: {{carer}} catches the spoon before it lands. You squeal with delight. This was meant to discourage you.

choices.label: Give it back with your sweetest smile

outcome.text: {{carer}} kisses your sticky forehead and lets you try feeding yourself. Most of supper reaches your mouth.

before.title: THE NIGHT INSPECTOR
before.text: {{carer}} has finally sat down. You open your eyes to check that the household remains properly staffed.

choices.label: Call for the night inspection

outcome.text: {{carer}} arrives with one shoe on the wrong foot. The inspection passes; the inspector remains unsatisfied.

choices.label: Settle to the sound of the chair

outcome.text: The chair creaks once more, then stops. {{carer}} gets a little rest without having to earn it twice.

after.title: EVERYONE SHOULD BE AWAKE
after.text: {{carer.intro}} has just fallen asleep in the chair beside you. One eye is still open. You would like the other one open too.

choices.label: Shout until both eyes open

outcome.text: {{carer}} lurches upright and bumps the table. You laugh so hard that a tired laugh comes back.

choices.label: Curl up and let them sleep

outcome.text: The chair creaks. {{carer}} sleeps with one hand on your blanket, and you drift off too.

before.title: THE FORTIFICATION OF SUPPER
before.text: You have arranged crusts round your bowl. {{carer}} attempts to introduce a spoon through an undefended gate.

choices.label: Defend the gate with both hands

outcome.text: The soup breaches the wall and most of your sleeve. {{carer}} admires the defence while removing the evidence.

choices.label: Let the spoon into the fortress

outcome.text: You eat. {{carer}} calls the siege a success and declines to discuss whose side won.

after.title: NO SPOONS ALLOWED
after.text: {{carer.intro}} brings your soup. You have built a wall of bread around the bowl and will not allow the spoon through.

choices.label: Slap away the invading spoon

outcome.text: Soup splashes down your sleeve. {{carer}} wipes you clean while you inspect the hole in your bread wall.

choices.label: Open a little gap

outcome.text: {{carer}} gets a spoonful past the bread. You eat it, look surprised, and allow another.

before.title: THE BOOT WITH A PASSENGER
before.text: You put a wooden toy inside {{carer}}’s boot. Departure now depends on a small creature accepting terms.

choices.label: Rescue the toy proudly

outcome.text: {{carer}} thanks you for solving a problem in which you have shown unusually complete expertise.

choices.label: Pretend the boot has always lived there

outcome.text: {{carer}} tips out the toy and studies your perfectly serious face. The boot resumes ordinary work.

after.title: THE BOOT WITH A PASSENGER
after.text: A wooden duck fits neatly into {{carer.intro}}’s boot. You push it right down to the toe and wait to see what happens.

choices.label: Fetch your duck when the hopping starts

outcome.text: {{carer}} holds out the boot. You fish out the duck and get a grateful squeeze, though the hopping has stopped.

choices.label: Look as surprised as possible

outcome.text: {{carer}} shakes out the duck. You stare at it in amazement. It is the best acting you have managed so far.

before.title: THE LAUNDRY HEARING
before.text: {{carer}} proposes washing your face. You have not been consulted about the status of the dirt.

choices.label: Object with your whole body

outcome.text: You preserve one muddy cheek through extraordinary effort. {{carer}} wins the other by negotiation.

choices.label: Hold the clean cloth yourself

outcome.text: {{carer}} gives you one corner. Your face becomes cleaner and the floor rather less so.

after.title: THAT IS MY DIRT
after.text: {{carer.intro}} approaches with a wet cloth. You clamp both hands over the patch of mud you have been saving on your cheek.

choices.label: Wriggle like an eel

outcome.text: {{carer}} catches one cheek, then the other. You get muddy fingerprints on the clean one and earn a helpless laugh.

choices.label: Take a corner of the cloth

outcome.text: You scrub your chin while {{carer}} does the difficult parts. Water runs down your neck, but the dirt comes off.

before.title: THE THREAD YOU CAN REACH
before.text: {{carer}} mends a sleeve while you hold the spare thread. The household has placed considerable confidence in a small fist.

choices.label: Hold the thread carefully

outcome.text: {{carer}} finishes the stitch and thanks you as though the sleeve could not have survived without the help.

choices.label: Test whether the thread is firmly attached

outcome.text: It is not. {{carer}} starts again and gives you a shorter, less strategically important piece.

after.title: ONE VERY IMPORTANT THREAD
after.text: {{carer.intro}} gives you the thread to hold while a torn sleeve is mended. You watch the needle as though it might bite.

choices.label: Keep your fist still

outcome.text: {{carer}} finishes the sleeve and pulls it on to show you. You pat the new stitches and are thanked for helping.

choices.label: See how far the thread goes

outcome.text: Much farther than expected. {{carer}} catches the sleeve before it falls apart and gives you a spare length to tug.

before.title: THE NEW HEADMASTER
before.text: The children elect a goat after it eats the attendance register. {{teacher}} declares the election unlawful. {{peer}} says the goat already has a carrot and three votes of confidence.

choices.label: Support the teacher’s authority

outcome.text: {{teacher}} removes the carrot from the meeting. The new headmaster follows its principal source of legitimacy out of the yard.

choices.label: Defend the goat’s election

outcome.text: The goat eats the appeal. {{teacher}} concedes that its administration is unusually decisive.

choices.label: Reconstruct the register rather generously

outcome.text: You improve attendance by adding children who are not present and one unusually literate pig. {{teacher}} notices the pig first.

after.title: THE NEW HEADMASTER
after.text: A goat eats the lesson sheet. {{peer}} puts a cap on it and seats it in {{teacher.intro}}’s chair. The goat immediately eats the cap.

choices.label: Help {{teacher}} get the goat outside

outcome.text: {{teacher}} holds out a carrot. The goat abandons its chair, while {{peer}} finds you a clean lesson sheet.

choices.label: Let the goat teach the lesson

outcome.text: {{teacher}} waits for a sensible answer. The goat swallows the last bit of cap, and {{peer}} snorts so loudly that you start laughing too.

choices.label: Replace the register with generous new names

outcome.text: You add three absent children and a pig. {{teacher}} asks the pig to read aloud, then takes the pencil away from you.

before.title: THE FINGER THAT GAVE EVIDENCE
before.text: {{teacher}} asks who touched the ink. {{peer}} recommends denying it before you remember which hand is black.

choices.label: Raise the guilty hand

outcome.text: {{teacher}} gives you a cleaning cloth. The lesson begins with a remarkably well-supported confession.

choices.label: Hide the hand behind your back

outcome.text: You leave a black handprint on your tunic. {{peer}} admires evidence that can travel with its owner.

after.title: THE HAND BEHIND YOUR BACK
after.text: {{teacher.intro}} finds an open inkpot. {{peer}} looks at your blackened hand, then at your face. “Put it in your pocket,” comes the whispered advice.

choices.label: Hold up the inky hand

outcome.text: {{teacher}} hands you a rag. You clean the spill together, and next time the inkpot is left within your reach.

choices.label: Hide it behind your back

outcome.text: You press a perfect black handprint onto your tunic. {{peer}} stuffs a sleeve into their mouth to stop laughing.

before.title: THE COURT WITHOUT A SECOND STOOL
before.text: {{peer}} holds court because their household owns the stool. The accused owns the biscuits.

choices.label: Hear the charge before the biscuits

outcome.text: The court hears an excellent case and receives no biscuits. {{peer}} asks whether justice is always this hungry.

choices.label: Propose a biscuit settlement

outcome.text: The accused distributes the evidence. {{peer}} declares the case deliciously inconclusive.

after.title: WHO GETS THE STOOL?
after.text: {{peer.intro}} gets the only stool and decides that means choosing every game. The rest of you have a plate of biscuits.

choices.label: Insist everyone gets a turn

outcome.text: {{peer}} listens to each child in turn. By the time a game is chosen, the biscuits are gone.

choices.label: Offer a biscuit for a turn on the stool

outcome.text: {{peer}} takes the biscuit and climbs down. You sit for a minute before sharing it out again.

before.title: THE BOAT THAT HAS NO INTEREST IN COMMAND
before.text: You and {{peer}} launch a wooden boat in a ditch. It immediately joins a different fleet beneath the bridge.

choices.label: Fetch it with a stick

outcome.text: You recover the boat and lose a sleeve to the mud. {{peer}} appoints you admiral of the stick.

choices.label: Charge spectators for the launch

outcome.text: {{peer}} demands a refund on behalf of the spectators. The spectators are three children and one unmoved dog.

after.title: THE BOAT THAT HAS NO INTEREST IN COMMAND
after.text: You and {{peer.intro}} launch a wooden boat in the ditch. It shoots under a bridge that neither of you can crawl beneath.

choices.label: Fish it out with a stick

outcome.text: You hook the boat and soak your sleeve. {{peer}} holds your belt so you do not follow it into the ditch.

choices.label: Make the other children pay to watch

outcome.text: The boat vanishes before your grand demonstration. {{peer}} has to return the pebbles while you explain the invisible ship.

before.title: THE CAKE RESERVED FOR A SAINT
before.text: {{peer}} finds a cake set aside for the parish celebration. The saint has not yet arrived to object.

choices.label: Guard it until the feast

outcome.text: {{peer}} helps guard the cake. Both guards are paid in slices after the duty is over.

choices.label: Taste only enough to establish its quality

outcome.text: The testing spreads to the other side of the cake. {{peer}} suggests calling the missing part an offering.

after.title: THE CAKE RESERVED FOR A SAINT
after.text: {{peer.intro}} lifts the cloth over a cake saved for the parish feast. There is a great deal of cake and nobody in the room but you.

choices.label: Cover it and wait for the feast

outcome.text: You both wait. The first slices reach you warm, and {{peer}} nudges yours across with the larger corner.

choices.label: Try a little from the far side

outcome.text: You and {{peer}} keep cutting it straight. When the cloth goes back, it sags into a hole big enough to hide a kitten.

before.title: THE BUTTON AT THE CENTRE OF THE WORLD
before.text: {{peer}} has lost a prized button in the rushes. Finding it has become more important than anything adults claim to be doing.

choices.label: Search carefully together

outcome.text: You find a bone bead, a nail and finally the button. {{peer}} keeps the button and gives you the bead.

choices.label: Claim you can find it for a reward

outcome.text: {{peer}} produces the button from another pocket before your demonstration. Your confidence remains for sale with fewer customers.

after.title: THE BUTTON AT THE CENTRE OF THE WORLD
after.text: {{peer.intro}} has lost a shiny button in the rushes. They are trying very hard not to cry, which makes finding it much more urgent.

choices.label: Get down and search together

outcome.text: You find a bead, a nail and the button. {{peer}} presses the bead into your hand and keeps checking that the button is still there.

choices.label: Promise to find it for a reward

outcome.text: {{peer}} reaches into another pocket and finds it. You pretend you were about to suggest looking there.

before.title: THE APPLE THAT DISPROVES THE SUM
before.text: {{teacher}} explains division using apples. {{peer}} is performing subtraction from the far end of the bench.

choices.label: Count the evidence before it vanishes

outcome.text: {{teacher}} changes the lesson to subtraction and asks {{peer}} to supply the answer. The answer is full.

choices.label: Help reduce the difficult numbers

outcome.text: The arithmetic becomes easy and the teacher becomes difficult. {{peer}} shares the last piece before the examples are confiscated.

after.title: THE APPLE THAT DISPROVES THE SUM
after.text: {{teacher.intro}} lays out apples for a lesson. At the far end of the bench, {{peer}} quietly makes one of the numbers smaller.

choices.label: Point out the missing apple

outcome.text: {{teacher}} asks {{peer}} to count aloud. A mouth full of apple makes this a difficult exercise.

choices.label: Help eat the difficult numbers

outcome.text: {{peer}} slips you a piece. {{teacher}} takes away the apples and gives you both more sums, which are much harder to swallow.

before.title: THE WORD YOU WERE NOT MEANT TO LEARN
before.text: {{carer}} uses a splendid new word after dropping a pot. {{peer}} asks whether you can remember it.

choices.label: Ask its meaning quietly

outcome.text: {{carer}} explains that the word is not useful at chapel. {{peer}} is disappointed by such a limited application.

choices.label: Demonstrate it at full volume

outcome.text: The word reaches three neighbours before {{carer}} reaches you. {{peer}} has acquired a favourite new quotation.

after.title: THE WORD YOU WERE NOT MEANT TO LEARN
after.text: {{carer.intro}} drops a pot and shouts a word you have never heard. {{peer}} leans close. “Say it again.”

choices.label: Ask what it means, quietly

outcome.text: {{carer}} tells you what it means and asks you not to repeat it at chapel. {{peer}} looks as though chapel has just become interesting.

choices.label: Try the new word at full volume

outcome.text: A neighbour drops a spoon. {{carer}} covers your mouth too late, while {{peer}} bends double laughing.

before.title: THE TOLL AT THE VERY SMALL BRIDGE
before.text: {{peer}} charges a pebble to cross a plank over a puddle. The bypass is one ordinary step.

choices.label: Walk round the puddle

outcome.text: {{peer}} announces a wider jurisdiction. You take a wider step.

choices.label: Offer to become deputy collector

outcome.text: The takings reach six pebbles before the owner of the plank asks for it back. {{peer}} gives you a glowing reference.

after.title: ONE PEBBLE TO CROSS
after.text: {{peer.intro}} wants a pebble from anyone crossing a plank over a puddle. You can get around the entire puddle in one step.

choices.label: Step around it

outcome.text: {{peer}} drags the plank to block you. You go around the other end. This continues until both of you are laughing.

choices.label: Help collect the pebbles

outcome.text: You collect six before an adult takes back the plank. {{peer}} lets you keep half the pebbles and blames the adult.

before.title: THE BELL THAT RINGS FOR BISCUITS
before.text: {{peer}} finds a small bell and proposes summoning the entire household to supper. Nobody has made supper.

choices.label: Return the bell before the announcement

outcome.text: The household remains undisturbed. {{peer}} says you have no appreciation of ceremony.

choices.label: Announce the excellent imaginary supper

outcome.text: Three adults arrive with impressive speed. {{peer}} discovers that the bell does not also produce food.

after.title: THE BELL THAT RINGS FOR BISCUITS
after.text: {{peer.intro}} finds a small bell. One ring could bring the whole household running to supper, if anybody had cooked it yet.

choices.label: Put it back before trouble comes

outcome.text: {{peer}} sighs, but helps you return it. The adults finish their work without being dragged away from it.

choices.label: Ring for a splendid imaginary supper

outcome.text: Three hungry adults arrive. {{peer}} looks into an empty bowl and whispers, “Ring it again. Perhaps that makes the food.”

before.title: THE INSPECTION OF THE IMPORTANT POCKET
before.text: {{carer}} empties your pocket before washing your clothes. The inventory includes a smooth stone, a bent nail and something that has accepted neither name nor explanation.

choices.label: Explain each treasure before sorting it

outcome.text: {{carer}} keeps the stone and removes the nail. The unidentified object is granted a hearing outside, with a shovel.

choices.label: Rescue the unidentified object first

outcome.text: It unfolds. {{carer}} opens the door and allows your collection to leave under its own power.

after.title: DO NOT WASH MY POCKET
after.text: {{carer.intro}} empties your pocket before washing your clothes. Out come a stone, a bent nail and something with far too many legs.

choices.label: Explain which things you need

outcome.text: {{carer}} lets you keep the stone. The nail goes on a high shelf and the many-legged treasure goes outside on a shovel.

choices.label: Grab the many-legged treasure

outcome.text: It scuttles up your sleeve. {{carer}} helps shake it out while you discover how quickly you can dance.

before.title: THE TRANSLATION THAT IMPROVES THE COOK
before.text: {{teacher}} assigns a Latin line. {{peer}} translates it as a command to give scholars better pudding.

choices.label: Check the difficult word

outcome.text: The line concerns patience. {{teacher}} describes the translation as a practical opportunity to demonstrate it.

choices.label: Defend the nourishing translation

outcome.text: {{teacher}} asks for the grammatical reason. {{peer}} supplies an excellent account of hunger and no grammar.

after.title: THE TRANSLATION THAT IMPROVES THE COOK
after.text: {{teacher.intro}} sets a Latin sentence. {{peer}} reads it as “give the children more pudding” and waits hopefully.

choices.label: Check the word for pudding

outcome.text: The word means patience. {{teacher}} makes you find the right passage, while {{peer}} keeps a finger on the wrong one.

choices.label: Explain why pudding fits the meaning

outcome.text: {{teacher}} asks for the grammar. {{peer}} rubs an empty stomach. It is a strong argument for lunch, but a poor one for Latin.

before.title: THE NICKNAME THAT HAS OUTLIVED THE JOKE
before.text: {{peer}} gives you a name the younger children repeat without understanding. They are very diligent pupils.

choices.label: Ask plainly for it to stop

outcome.text: {{peer}} sees that you are not performing for the audience. The next attempt at the joke is quieter and much less certain.

choices.label: Invent a crueler name in return

outcome.text: The audience learns two names. {{peer}} begins collecting examples, and the game stops feeling like one.

after.title: THE NICKNAME THAT HAS OUTLIVED THE JOKE
after.text: {{peer.intro}} gives you an unkind nickname. Younger children start repeating it, even when you are close enough to hear every word.

choices.label: Tell them it hurts and ask them to stop

outcome.text: {{peer}} glances at your face and drops the grin. The next time somebody repeats it, they change the subject.

choices.label: Find a crueler name for them

outcome.text: The younger children learn both names. {{peer}} stops laughing and starts using yours whenever an adult turns away.

before.title: THE HOUSEHOLD’S FIRST REAL ACCOUNT
before.text: {{carer}} lets you compare the household tally with the goods. The tally is much more optimistic.

choices.label: Name the shortage carefully

outcome.text: {{carer}} changes the supper plan without blaming your arithmetic. The household has learned something useful before it becomes hungry.

choices.label: Make the account look reassuring

outcome.text: {{carer}} finds the empty shelf. Your figures are moved to the category of things that require checking.

after.title: THE HOUSEHOLD’S FIRST REAL ACCOUNT
after.text: {{carer.intro}} asks you to count the grain sacks. There are fewer than the tally says, and the empty shelf is hard to argue with.

choices.label: Show where the grain is missing

outcome.text: {{carer}} checks the shelf and changes the supper plan. Your careful count leaves a little more grain for the lean week ahead.

choices.label: Write down the reassuring number

outcome.text: {{carer}} finds the bare shelf later and recounts everything. Next time, you have to count with someone watching.

before.title: THE BRIDGE PLAN DRAWN AFTER THE RAIN
before.text: {{peer}} proposes building a footbridge from spare boards. The drawing includes a heroic figure in a cloak, but no supports.

choices.label: Add the boring necessary supports

outcome.text: {{peer}} removes the cloak to make room on the slate. The model now stands without needing anyone to be brave.

choices.label: Keep the heroic figure and test the model

outcome.text: The model folds beneath a pebble. {{peer}} moves the hero to the bank, where command appears much safer.

after.title: THE BRIDGE PLAN DRAWN AFTER THE RAIN
after.text: {{peer.intro}} draws a bridge to build from spare boards. There is room for a hero in a cloak, but nothing holding up the middle.

choices.label: Make room for the supports

outcome.text: {{peer}} rubs out the cloak. With two extra supports, your little model stays upright and the bridge might be useful.

choices.label: Test the heroic version

outcome.text: One pebble folds the bridge in half. {{peer}} redraws the hero on the bank, well away from the water.

before.title: THE LETTER THAT HAS MET ITS READER
before.text: {{peer}} has read your carefully composed note and asks whether the excellent handwriting is meant to distract from the question.

choices.label: Ask honestly and accept the answer

outcome.text: You manage a conversation without borrowed verses. {{peer}} answers without inviting the lane to judge it.

choices.label: Claim you were copying an exercise

outcome.text: {{peer}} asks which lesson requires quite so many compliments about their eyes. The handwriting is admired at a distance.

after.title: THE LETTER THAT HAS MET ITS READER
after.text: {{peer.intro}} has your note. They point to the line about their eyes and wait for you to stop staring at your shoes.

choices.label: Ask the question you meant to ask

outcome.text: You get the words out without a borrowed verse. {{peer}} answers quietly, and neither of you has to involve the whole lane.

choices.label: Say it was a handwriting exercise

outcome.text: {{peer}} reads the line about their eyes again. You decide to become very interested in the weather.

before.title: THE WAGE WITH AN INVISIBLE DEDUCTION
before.text: {{other}} offers your first paid errand, less a fee for teaching you the privilege of being paid.

choices.label: Ask for the actual wage before agreeing

outcome.text: {{other}} removes the instructional fee after discovering you have understood that part without tuition.

choices.label: Accept the bad bargain for experience

outcome.text: You receive two gold and a lesson worth at least the missing two. {{other}} praises your cooperative nature.

after.title: THE WAGE WITH AN INVISIBLE DEDUCTION
after.text: {{other.intro}} offers to pay you for an errand, then takes back half the wage as a fee for learning how to do it.

choices.label: Ask for the whole wage before you start

outcome.text: {{other}} grumbles, but pays four gold. You do the errand carefully; you would like to be paid again.

choices.label: Take the two gold and get it done

outcome.text: You carry the sack and collect two gold. {{other}} pats your shoulder and asks whether the free instructions made it a fair bargain.

before.title: THE BOOK THAT SHOULD NOT BE THIS INTERESTING
before.text: {{peer}} finds a forbidden page in a respectable book. The author has helpfully marked the exciting parts in red.

choices.label: Read it critically rather than circulate it

outcome.text: You identify the argument and its weaknesses. {{peer}} is disappointed to discover that scandal can require homework.

choices.label: Copy the red parts for everyone

outcome.text: The copies are traced by your distinctive red initials. {{peer}} suggests that anonymity might have required another colour.

after.title: THE BOOK THAT SHOULD NOT BE THIS INTERESTING
after.text: {{peer.intro}} opens a respectable book at a forbidden page. Somebody has underlined all the exciting parts in red.

choices.label: Read the argument and check it

outcome.text: You find a flaw in the passage and point it out. {{peer}} groans; you have somehow made forbidden reading into more work.

choices.label: Copy the red bits for everyone

outcome.text: The copies are traced to your enormous red initials. {{peer}} quietly turns your name face down.

before.title: THE REFERENCE WRITTEN BY ITS BENEFICIARY
before.text: {{peer}} has written you a glowing reference for work. It praises three skills you do not yet possess and a fourth that nobody recognises.

choices.label: Correct the reference before using it

outcome.text: {{peer}} keeps one compliment you can defend. The employer receives a smaller promise and a more useful applicant.

choices.label: Submit the magnificent version

outcome.text: The employer asks for a demonstration of the mysterious fourth skill. {{peer}} is suddenly unavailable to explain it.

after.title: THE REFERENCE WRITTEN BY ITS BENEFICIARY
after.text: {{peer.intro}} writes you a glowing reference. It lists three skills you do not have and one that neither of you can pronounce.

choices.label: Leave in the things you can actually do

outcome.text: {{peer}} keeps one warm compliment and crosses out the rest. The shorter reference gives you something you can build on.

choices.label: Hand over the magnificent version

outcome.text: You are asked to demonstrate the unpronounceable skill. {{peer}} takes a sudden interest in a very distant part of the yard.

before.title: SILENCE AT THE MARKET RATE
before.text: Your rival {{other}} offers silence about a rumour. The offer is made loudly enough to demonstrate what the money would buy.

choices.label: Refuse the bargain

outcome.text: {{other}} raises the voice, then remembers everyone can now hear the price as well.

choices.label: Describe the demand publicly

outcome.text: You repeat the offer exactly. {{other}} objects to the lack of discretion in your account of extortion.

after.title: SILENCE AT THE MARKET RATE
after.text: {{other.intro}} offers to stop repeating a rumour about you. The price is shouted across the market. So is the rumour.

choices.label: Refuse to buy the silence

outcome.text: {{other}} shouts a higher price. Several listeners ask whether shouting costs extra.

choices.label: Repeat the offer to everyone listening

outcome.text: You quote the demand word for word. {{other}} discovers how embarrassing it is to have an exact price put on their discretion.

before.title: THE ANCESTOR WITH TWO EXCLUSIVE FAMILIES
before.text: {{other}} offers an exclusive pedigree also displayed on a neighbouring stall. The ancestor appears to have reproduced chiefly through commissions.

choices.label: Withdraw the doubtful claim

outcome.text: {{other}} asks whether a smaller ancestor at a lower price might suit.

choices.label: Defend the descent under oath

outcome.text: The clerk asks where you met the witness from 1180. {{other}} has stopped offering introductions.

charge.offence: Defending an invented pedigree under oath

after.title: THE ANCESTOR WITH TWO EXCLUSIVE FAMILIES
after.text: {{other.intro}} tries to sell you an exclusive pedigree. Two stalls away, the same ancestor has six different descendants and a cheaper frame.

choices.label: Drop the doubtful claim

outcome.text: {{other}} offers a smaller ancestor at half the price. You leave before the family shrinks any further.

choices.label: Swear the pedigree is true

outcome.text: The clerk asks how you met the witness from 1180. {{other}} suddenly has another customer to serve.

charge.offence: Defending an invented pedigree under oath

before.title: THE LUNCH COLLECTOR HAS LOST THE BADGE
before.text: {{other}} collects lunches for the older children. The badge is a leaf, and the older children deny employing a leaf.

choices.label: Agree to stop the collection

outcome.text: {{other}} drops the badge. You leave the lunches where their owners can reach them.

choices.label: Demand lunch as repayment

outcome.text: {{other}} recognises the method. You have abolished the collector by taking the job.

after.title: THE LUNCH COLLECTOR HAS LOST THE BADGE
after.text: {{other.intro}} takes the other children’s lunches while wearing a leaf as a badge. The oldest children deny sending anyone with a leaf.

choices.label: Stop taking lunches together

outcome.text: {{other}} pulls off the leaf. You both leave the food where its owners can reach it.

choices.label: Demand a lunch as repayment

outcome.text: {{other}} hands it over and looks at you with weary recognition. The leaf is gone, but the children are still losing their lunch.

before.title: THE GRIEVANCE WITHOUT THE GLOVE
before.text: Roderick arrives to state a grievance in words. {{other}} has left the glove at home and regards this as a considerable concession.

choices.label: Hear him without an audience

outcome.text: Roderick finishes without applause or a weapon. The grievance shrinks when nobody is performing it.

choices.label: Give your best answer publicly

outcome.text: Roderick produces the glove after all. It was in the other pocket, with several less patient sentences.

after.title: THE GRIEVANCE WITHOUT THE GLOVE
after.text: {{other.intro}} arrives to tell you exactly what he thinks of you. He says he left his duelling glove at home and shows you both empty hands.

choices.label: Hear Roderick without an audience

outcome.text: Roderick gets through the complaint without reaching for a weapon. Once you answer quietly, he finds rather less to shout about.

choices.label: Give your finest answer in public

outcome.text: Roderick produces the glove. It was in the other pocket. Your audience takes a quick, interested step backward.

before.title: THE GUARANTEE FITS IN THE BOTTLE
before.text: {{other}} offers a guarantee promising only that the bottle contains tonic. The lettering is much smaller than “guarantee”.

choices.label: Welcome the limited honest claim

outcome.text: {{other}} lists ingredients without offering to rearrange your future. The smaller promise is refreshing.

choices.label: Decline without another argument

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts that an honest label does not create a thirsty customer.

after.title: THE GUARANTEE FITS IN THE BOTTLE
after.text: {{other.intro}} points to a tonic’s guarantee. It promises that the bottle contains tonic. The ingredients appear in much smaller writing.

choices.label: Accept a plain account of what is in it

outcome.text: {{other}} reads the ingredients without promising to restore your youth or rearrange your teeth. You can finally judge the offer itself.

choices.label: Decline it without another argument

outcome.text: {{other}} puts the bottle away. You leave with your coins and the teeth you arrived with.

before.title: THE VICTORY BOW BEFORE THE RACE
before.text: {{other}} has challenged you before witnesses, drawn the finish line and rehearsed a victory bow. The race has not yet acquired a second willing participant.

choices.label: Accept the challenge

success.text: You finish first. {{other}} delivers the rehearsed bow to entirely the wrong audience.

failure.text: You finish behind {{other}}, but well ahead of the sack you were supposed to carry. The crowd generously counts this as two competitions.

choices.label: Make the rules public before agreeing

outcome.text: The witnesses reject three of {{other}}’s rules and the foot planted on your starting line. The contest is abandoned on grounds of sudden fatigue.

choices.label: Carry the load together instead

outcome.text: {{other}} objects to being pitied, then accepts the other handle. Neither of you wins; the intended owner finally receives the sack.

after.title: THE VICTORY BOW BEFORE THE RACE
after.text: {{other.intro}} draws a finish line and practises a victory bow. Then they invite you to race. Several people have stopped to see whether the bow was premature.

choices.label: Race for it

success.text: You finish first. {{other}} bows automatically, sees you beside them, and wishes they had not practised so thoroughly.

failure.text: {{other}} beats you to the line. You arrive breathless with a sore leg, and the grin waiting for you is larger than the crowd.

choices.label: Check the rules before agreeing

outcome.text: {{other}} has given themselves a shorter course and the good starting spot. You point this out, and the race is suddenly far less urgent.

choices.label: Carry the sack together instead

outcome.text: {{other}} takes the other handle after a little grumbling. Your shoulders ache, but the sack reaches its owner and you part on better terms.

before.title: THE WILL WITH ROOM FOR ANOTHER SIGNATURE
before.text: {{other}} claims the household inheritance. The witness has helpfully left a blank beside the signature, in case the dead should wish to improve the arrangement.

choices.label: Contest the claim before witnesses (9g)

outcome.text: The witnessed inventory puts the disputed goods beyond {{other}}’s reach. The clerk charges for the copy and, after a pause, for the original being correct.

choices.label: Negotiate a division now

outcome.text: You surrender part of the goods and end the claim in writing. {{other}} accepts, having discovered that a smaller inheritance weighs less than another argument.

choices.label: Fill the blank yourself

outcome.text: Your version is wonderfully clear and legally disastrous. {{other}} recognises the ink, and the clerk finally has a document worth investigating.

choices.label: Surrender the disputed goods

outcome.text: The goods leave with {{other}}. You close the door on the argument and stand for a while where the better chest used to be.

after.title: THE WILL WITH ROOM FOR ANOTHER SIGNATURE
after.text: {{other.intro}} wants your household’s inheritance. The proposed settlement leaves a blank beside the witness’s name. A fresh quill lies helpfully across it.

choices.label: Pay nine gold to contest the claim

outcome.text: The witnesses identify the disputed goods and your household keeps them. {{other}} leaves angry, while the clerk counts the nine-gold fee twice.

choices.label: Agree a smaller share now

outcome.text: You give up some goods and have the settlement witnessed. {{other}} helps carry the agreed share instead of returning with another demand.

choices.label: Fill in the helpful blank

outcome.text: You secure the larger share until {{other}} recognises your handwriting. The forgery gives the authorities something concrete to investigate.

choices.label: Give up the disputed goods

outcome.text: {{other}} carries the goods away. You hold the door, accept the quiet thanks and shut it on an emptier room.

before.title: THE BED THAT HAS BECOME A PEDIGREE
before.text: {{sibling}} claims the best bed as the elder child. The argument has acquired three ancestors, two doubtful customs and no spare mattress.

choices.label: Agree a witnessed division

outcome.text: You accept fewer goods in exchange for a final settlement. {{sibling}} signs before an ancestor can be found who slept on the floor.

choices.label: Give the bed and keep the relationship

outcome.text: {{sibling}} sits on the bed and, after an awkward pause, asks you to stay for supper.

choices.label: Produce a more convenient family inventory

outcome.text: The inventory is convincing until {{sibling}} remembers carving the listed chest last winter. A forgery complaint replaces the question of blankets.

after.title: THE BED THAT HAS BECOME A PEDIGREE
after.text: {{sibling.intro}} lies across the best bed and will not move. You are trying to divide the household goods. They suggest beginning with something they are not lying on.

choices.label: Agree a division with witnesses

outcome.text: You take fewer goods and get the division witnessed. {{sibling}} finally sits up, trusts the agreement and helps carry your share.

choices.label: Let them have the bed

outcome.text: {{sibling}} smooths the blanket, then notices you still standing. They make room for you to sit and ask you to stay for supper.

choices.label: Invent a better inventory for yourself

outcome.text: You get the larger share until {{sibling}} recognises the chest they carved last winter. They take the false list to the authorities.

before.title: THE COPE-CHEST HAS ACQUIRED A DEADLINE
before.text: {{other}} wants an oak chest, a lower price and an earlier delivery. The apprentice’s better joint is described as an unacceptable innovation until the old one splits.

choices.label: Use the apprentice’s joint and name the work honestly

outcome.text: The chest closes squarely. {{other}} tries to complain about the method and is defeated by the lid.

choices.label: Use cheap timber and conceal the split

outcome.text: You pocket the difference. {{other}} finds the split when the chest is lifted; the receipt is stronger than the wood.

choices.label: Return the advance rather than the promise (8g)

outcome.text: You return the advance and keep your tools. {{other}} takes the schedule to someone whose timber is apparently more obedient.

after.title: THE COPE-CHEST HAS ACQUIRED A DEADLINE
after.text: {{other.intro}} wants an oak chest finished by tomorrow. Their purse contains next week’s price. An apprentice shows you a better joint as the old sample splits on the bench.

choices.label: Use the sound joint and credit the apprentice

outcome.text: The lid closes neatly. {{other}} tries to lift the chest by one corner, fails to break it, and pays eight gold with obvious reluctance.

choices.label: Hide a split in cheap timber

outcome.text: You pocket eighteen gold. {{other}} lifts the chest, sees daylight through the split, and carries the receipt straight to the guild.

choices.label: Give back the eight-gold advance

outcome.text: {{other}} takes the money back and complains about the delay. You keep your tools, your unbroken timber and one fewer impossible promise.

before.title: THE DRIVER RETURNS WITHOUT THE CART
before.text: {{other}} returns with no cart and an account containing a bridge, a lord and an extremely powerful pig. The freight receipt mentions none of them.

choices.label: Compare the route, witnesses and receipts

outcome.text: The story loses its lord, then its bridge. The pig survives as a regrettable error in loading, for which {{other}} accepts responsibility.

choices.label: Accept a partial repayment now

outcome.text: {{other}} pays eight gold and signs for the missing goods. The pig is left out of the agreement to save parchment.

after.title: THE DRIVER RETURNS WITHOUT THE CART
after.text: {{other.intro}} returns without your cart. They blame a bridge, a lord and a pig powerful enough to overturn both. You ask which part happened first.

choices.label: Check the route and talk to people who saw it

outcome.text: The lord disappears from the story, then the bridge. {{other}} admits overloading the cart and returns some of the missing goods.

choices.label: Take eight gold back now

outcome.text: {{other}} counts out eight gold. You acknowledge the payment, but refuse to put the pig’s alleged title in writing.

before.title: THE HOUSEHOLD’S NEW BAILIFF
before.text: {{child}} has begun charging visitors a toll of buttons. A visiting neighbour has paid in order to find out what happens next.

choices.label: Make the little collector restore every button

outcome.text: {{child}} returns the buttons under supervision. The household loses an afternoon and gains an accountant who now understands refunds.

choices.label: Declare the doorstep a lawful little manor

outcome.text: You defend the toll. The household’s standing falls, but {{child}} gains confidence in the hereditary nature of nonsense.

choices.label: Turn the whole levy into a counting lesson

outcome.text: You replace the toll with a game that gives the buttons back. {{child}} discovers that rules can be improved without conquering the neighbours.

after.title: THE HOUSEHOLD’S NEW BAILIFF
after.text: {{child.intro}} has stretched a string across the doorstep. Visitors must pay a button to get in. A neighbour is already missing one and wants to see where this leads.

choices.label: Help return every button

outcome.text: {{child}} knocks on the neighbours’ doors with you and returns the buttons. One coat is fastened again before you get home.

choices.label: Back your child and keep charging

outcome.text: {{child}} beams at your support. The neighbours stop visiting, and somebody cuts the string while you are inside.

choices.label: Make it a counting game with no real toll

outcome.text: You put the buttons in a pile and count them with {{child}}, then give them back. The child tries to count the neighbours too.

before.title: THE LADDER THAT IS NEVER HOME
before.text: {{other}} has borrowed your household’s ladder so often that visitors now ask directions to it rather than to you.

choices.label: Retrieve it and help finish the repair

outcome.text: You bring the ladder home after helping with the roof. {{other}} owes you a kindness, and the household can reach its own rafters again.

choices.label: Charge for this year’s use (5g)

outcome.text: {{other}} pays five gold and becomes much less neighbourly. The ladder has earned more than most apprentices.

choices.label: Give it away and make a lower set of shelves

outcome.text: {{other}} takes the ladder home permanently. You lower the shelves and stop receiving requests to borrow your furniture’s only means of escape.

after.title: THE LADDER THAT IS NEVER HOME
after.text: {{other.intro}} has your ladder again. Their roof is mended. Your ladder is now holding up a washing line.

choices.label: Help finish up and carry it home

outcome.text: You climb up to free the line, then carry the ladder home together. Your shoulders ache, but you can finally repair your own rafters.

choices.label: Ask for five gold for all that borrowing

outcome.text: {{other}} hands over five gold and takes the washing down very slowly. The next greeting across the lane is much shorter.

choices.label: Let them keep it and lower your shelves

outcome.text: {{other}} carries it away with both hands and a grin. You move the high shelves down and gain a friend who no longer needs an excuse to call.

before.title: THE CONDITIONAL BLESSING
before.text: {{child}} has written a promise to obey you “where reasonably convenient.” It has been copied beautifully.

choices.label: Discuss what convenient actually means

outcome.text: You agree on chores and limits. {{child}} keeps the phrase in the copy, now accompanied by a rather demanding definition.

choices.label: Tear up the qualifying words

outcome.text: You enforce obedience and damage trust. {{child}} learns to leave a wider margin for thoughts you will not read.

after.title: THE CONDITIONAL BLESSING
after.text: {{child.intro}} writes a promise to obey you, then adds “when I am not busy.” The handwriting is much neater around those last six words.

choices.label: Agree which chores come before being busy

outcome.text: You work through the chores together. {{child}} grumbles over two, agrees to the rest, and lets you keep the finished copy.

choices.label: Tear off the qualifying words

outcome.text: {{child}} takes back the torn sheet. The next promise is shorter and leaves out everything you might disagree with.

before.title: THE BAILIFF’S FOURTH CHICKEN
before.text: The bailiff demands a hen that your household has never owned. Your family contact has the old rent tally.

choices.label: Compare the bailiff’s rent tally

outcome.text: You and your neighbour prove the tally. The hen remains imaginary; the debt does not grow.

choices.label: Accept the bailiff’s hush money

outcome.text: The bailiff pays you three coins to hide his extra assessment. Your household loses more grain than those coins could buy.

after.title: THE BAILIFF’S FOURTH CHICKEN
after.text: The bailiff demands a fourth hen. {{guardian.intro}} has counted three since you were small. You are sent to fetch the old tally before anyone catches a bird.

choices.label: Compare the bailiff’s rent tally

outcome.text: {{contact}} helps you check the tally. Three hens remain three hens, and {{guardian}} takes them back to the yard.

choices.label: Accept the bailiff’s hush money

outcome.text: The bailiff pays you three coins to hide his extra assessment. Your household loses more grain than those coins could buy.

before.title: THE GUILD’S SMALL PRINT
before.text: Your family’s commission includes a penalty for hammer noise after compline. The church commissioned the bell.

choices.label: Ask {{contact}} to check the guild exemption

outcome.text: The guild contact finds the exemption. The collector departs without the fee and with a much lower opinion of children being taught to read.

choices.label: Keep the noise penalty secret for three gold

outcome.text: You pocket three gold while the workshop pays the penalty. {{contact}} learns whose silence was purchased.

after.title: THE GUILD’S SMALL PRINT
after.text: Your household is being fined for hammering after compline. {{guardian.intro}} points at the bell you are making for the church. It will be much quieter if nobody finishes it.

choices.label: Ask {{contact}} to check the guild exemption

outcome.text: {{contact}} finds the exemption for the church’s own bell. {{guardian}} gets back to work while the collector discovers somewhere else to be.

choices.label: Keep the noise penalty secret for three gold

outcome.text: You pocket three gold while the workshop pays the penalty. {{contact}} learns whose silence was purchased.

before.title: THE RIVAL’S SHORT BUSHEL
before.text: The household’s rival sells grain in a bushel with a false bottom. Your parent asks you to watch the measure.

choices.label: Ask {{contact}} to witness the false measure

outcome.text: You bring witnesses and protect the household’s buyers. The rival now knows your name.

choices.label: Take three gold from the short-measure seller

outcome.text: The seller buys your silence. Your household’s buyers discover the short grain and blame the family name.

after.title: THE RIVAL’S SHORT BUSHEL
after.text: A seller’s grain measure has a false bottom. {{guardian.intro}} asks you to watch it filled. The seller keeps putting a large hand over the part you want to see.

choices.label: Ask {{contact}} to witness the false measure

outcome.text: {{contact}} witnesses the measure being emptied. Your household’s buyers keep their grain, and the seller stops waving you nearer.

choices.label: Take three gold from the short-measure seller

outcome.text: The seller buys your silence. Your household’s buyers discover the short grain and blame the family name.

before.title: THE LAY SCRIBE’S BABY
before.text: A visiting friar mistakes your lay scribe parent for a vowed cleric and prepares a scandal of magnificent proportions.

choices.label: Produce the household marriage entry

outcome.text: The marriage entry settles it. The friar must find his scandal elsewhere.

choices.label: Sell the friar a rumour for three gold

outcome.text: The friar pays for a scandal about your own lay household. The correction will cost considerably more than three gold.

after.title: THE LAY SCRIBE’S BABY
after.text: A visiting friar sees a child’s toy beside the household books and leaps to a scandal. {{guardian.intro}} points out that lay scribes are allowed families. He has already drawn breath for the sermon.

choices.label: Produce the household marriage entry

outcome.text: {{contact}} helps produce the marriage entry. The friar shuts his mouth, opens it once more, and settles for asking directions.

choices.label: Sell the friar a rumour for three gold

outcome.text: The friar pays for a scandal about your own lay household. The correction will cost considerably more than three gold.

before.title: THE RATION HEIR
before.text: The garrison refuses to feed a soldier’s child until the child can carry a spear. The spear is taller than the clerk.

choices.label: Ask {{contact}} to cite the service oath

outcome.text: Your household receives its bread. The stores clerk hands over each loaf as though personally surrendering a small fort.

choices.label: Take three gold to abandon the ration claim

outcome.text: The stores clerk buys your silence. Your family gives up a season of bread for your private handful of coins.

after.title: THE RATION HEIR
after.text: The garrison will not feed a soldier’s child until the child can carry a spear. {{guardian.intro}} brings you forward. The spear is taller than the man refusing the bread.

choices.label: Ask {{contact}} to cite the service oath

outcome.text: {{contact}} helps establish the household’s right to rations. {{guardian}} takes the bread while the clerk tries not to look at the spear.

choices.label: Take three gold to abandon the ration claim

outcome.text: The stores clerk buys your silence. Your family gives up a season of bread for your private handful of coins.

before.title: THE COUSIN’S LITTLE MAP
before.text: A cousin has drawn the family boundary through your nursery. The steward offers to charge you rent.

choices.label: Ask {{contact}} to compare the boundary charter

outcome.text: You compare the charter with the stones. The cousin loses a field and a little affection.

choices.label: Accept three gold to hide the cousin’s map

outcome.text: Your cousin buys your silence and presses the boundary claim. The household discovers your price was lower than the surveyor’s.

after.title: THE COUSIN’S LITTLE MAP
after.text: A cousin’s new boundary map runs through your nursery. {{guardian.intro}} asks you to carry the old charter. The cousin has helpfully offered to rent the nursery back.

choices.label: Ask {{contact}} to compare the boundary charter

outcome.text: You and {{contact}} compare the charter with the boundary stones. {{guardian}} keeps the field, and the cousin takes back a very expensive drawing.

choices.label: Accept three gold to hide the cousin’s map

outcome.text: Your cousin buys your silence and presses the boundary claim. The household discovers your price was lower than the surveyor’s.

before.title: THE NURSERY PRECEDENT
before.text: Your older sibling claims the whole nursery under a succession custom invented before breakfast.

choices.label: Ask the guardian to settle nursery precedence

outcome.text: Your guardian divides the room. The throne remains undivided and very far away.

choices.label: Sell your sibling the secret nursery key

outcome.text: Your sibling pays three gold for the nursery key. The guards change the locks and your household’s opinion of you.

after.title: THE NURSERY PRECEDENT
after.text: Your elder sibling claims the whole nursery. {{guardian.intro}} asks on what grounds. “I got here first,” comes the answer from behind a barricade of cushions.

choices.label: Ask the guardian to settle nursery precedence

outcome.text: {{guardian}} divides the room and has you both move the cushions. {{contact}} watches the new border survive almost until supper.

choices.label: Sell your sibling the secret nursery key

outcome.text: Your sibling pays three gold for the nursery key. The guards change the locks and your household’s opinion of you.

before.title: THE FLOODED STRIP
before.text: {{guardian}} finds seed floating across a neighbour’s boundary. {{contact}} remembers where the old ditch ran.

choices.label: Reopen the ditch together

outcome.text: The reopened ditch saves seed on both strips. {{contact}} records your household’s share of the labour.

choices.label: Charge the neighbour for your own lost seed

outcome.text: Your false claim wins a few coins and leaves {{guardian}} to repair the damaged neighbourly agreement.

after.title: THE FLOODED STRIP
after.text: Seed from {{guardian.intro}}’s strip is floating into the next field. {{contact}} points to the old ditch. You can see the boundary dispute sprouting.

choices.label: Reopen the ditch together

outcome.text: The reopened ditch saves seed on both strips. {{contact}} records your household’s share of the labour.

choices.label: Charge the neighbour for your own lost seed

outcome.text: Your false claim wins a few coins and leaves {{guardian}} to repair the damaged neighbourly agreement.

before.title: THE WINTER WOOD
before.text: {{contact}} offers fallen wood if your household helps mend the common gate before winter.

choices.label: Help {{guardian}} mend the gate

outcome.text: The common gate stands through winter. {{contact}} delivers the promised fallen wood.

choices.label: Sell the gate timber secretly

outcome.text: The missing timber leaves the common gate open. {{contact}} charges your household for its replacement.

after.title: THE WINTER WOOD
after.text: {{contact.intro}} offers fallen wood if your household helps repair the common gate. {{guardian}} looks at the cold hearth, then at your good clothes. You put on the other pair.

choices.label: Help {{guardian}} mend the gate

outcome.text: The common gate stands through winter. {{contact}} delivers the promised fallen wood.

choices.label: Sell the gate timber secretly

outcome.text: The missing timber leaves the common gate open. {{contact}} charges your household for its replacement.

before.title: THE CUSTOMER’S SEAL
before.text: {{guardian}} has a commission without a deposit. {{contact}} recognises the customer’s disputed seal.

choices.label: Ask for a witnessed deposit

outcome.text: The witnessed deposit pays for material before the customer can dispute the order.

choices.label: Copy the seal onto another order

outcome.text: The copied seal is discovered on the second order. {{contact}} keeps it as evidence against your household.

after.title: THE CUSTOMER’S SEAL
after.text: {{guardian.intro}} has begun a commission without a deposit. {{contact}} recognises the customer’s disputed seal. There is already a week’s work on the bench.

choices.label: Ask for a witnessed deposit

outcome.text: The witnessed deposit pays for material before the customer can dispute the order.

choices.label: Copy the seal onto another order

outcome.text: The copied seal is discovered on the second order. {{contact}} keeps it as evidence against your household.

before.title: THE GUILD FEAST
before.text: {{contact}} invites your household to show a trial piece. The entry fee will buy a week’s supper.

choices.label: Help {{guardian}} prepare a modest sample

outcome.text: The workshop’s sample is admired, tasted and promptly requested in a larger quantity. Your household still has supper when the important guests finish theirs.

choices.label: Pass off another workshop’s piece

outcome.text: The borrowed trial piece is recognised. Your workshop pays the entry fee and loses the guild’s trust.

after.title: THE GUILD FEAST
after.text: {{contact.intro}} invites the household to show a trial piece. {{guardian}} counts out an entry fee large enough to buy a week’s supper, then counts it again.

choices.label: Help {{guardian}} prepare a modest sample

outcome.text: The workshop’s sample is admired, tasted and promptly requested in a larger quantity. Your household still has supper when the important guests finish theirs.

choices.label: Pass off another workshop’s piece

outcome.text: The borrowed trial piece is recognised. Your workshop pays the entry fee and loses the guild’s trust.

before.title: THE SHIPMENT AT THE FORD
before.text: {{guardian}} must choose between a safe crossing fee and a cheap flooded ford. {{contact}} has a wagon there too.

choices.label: Share the safe crossing cost

outcome.text: Both wagons share the safe crossing and split the fee. The shipment arrives with its partners intact.

choices.label: Send {{contact}} toward the flooded ford

outcome.text: {{contact}} finds the dangerous ford and learns who gave the directions. Your household loses a trading partner.

after.title: THE SHIPMENT AT THE FORD
after.text: {{guardian.intro}} reaches a toll bridge with a wagon. {{contact}} is there too, staring at the cheap flooded ford. Only the bridge has a dry way across.

choices.label: Share the safe crossing cost

outcome.text: Both wagons share the safe crossing and split the fee. The shipment arrives with its partners intact.

choices.label: Send {{contact}} toward the flooded ford

outcome.text: {{contact}} finds the dangerous ford and learns who gave the directions. Your household loses a trading partner.

before.title: THE BORROWED MANUSCRIPT
before.text: {{guardian}} owes the priory a manuscript. {{contact}} finds rain beneath the reading-room window.

choices.label: Help dry and recopy the damaged leaves

outcome.text: The dried leaves and careful copies satisfy the priory. Your lay household retains its access to the books.

choices.label: Blame a visiting lay household

outcome.text: The visiting household produces witnesses. Your own household pays for the damaged manuscript.

after.title: THE BORROWED MANUSCRIPT
after.text: Rain creeps beneath the reading-room window onto a manuscript {{guardian.intro}} owes the priory. {{contact}} arrives to find you holding the book over your head.

choices.label: Help dry and recopy the damaged leaves

outcome.text: The dried leaves and careful copies satisfy the priory. Your lay household retains its access to the books.

choices.label: Blame a visiting lay household

outcome.text: The visiting household produces witnesses. Your own household pays for the damaged manuscript.

before.title: THE CHARITY BREAD
before.text: {{contact}} asks your household to record bread for hungry neighbours. One loaf remains after the tally.

choices.label: Ask {{guardian}} to check the names

outcome.text: The checked names reveal a hungry neighbour missed from the tally. The last loaf reaches them.

choices.label: Sell the extra loaf and alter the list

outcome.text: The altered bread list is traced to your hand. Your household must replace what the charity lost.

after.title: THE CHARITY BREAD
after.text: {{contact.intro}} asks for help recording bread for hungry neighbours. {{guardian}} checks the list. One loaf remains, and somebody is still waiting by the door.

choices.label: Ask {{guardian}} to check the names

outcome.text: The checked names reveal a hungry neighbour missed from the tally. The last loaf reaches them.

choices.label: Sell the extra loaf and alter the list

outcome.text: The altered bread list is traced to your hand. Your household must replace what the charity lost.

before.title: THE GARRISON’S HORSE
before.text: {{contact}} needs someone to hold a nervous horse while {{guardian}} checks its harness.

choices.label: Help check the girth and stay beside it

outcome.text: The checked girth holds and the garrison records your household’s help.

choices.label: Tell the quartermaster another child lost it

outcome.text: The quartermaster finds your false account beside the harness. Your household loses standing with the stores.

after.title: THE GARRISON’S HORSE
after.text: {{contact.intro}} needs help with a nervous horse while {{guardian}} checks its harness. The horse would prefer all of you to stop discussing it and stand farther away.

choices.label: Help check the girth and stay beside it

outcome.text: The checked girth holds and the garrison records your household’s help.

choices.label: Tell the quartermaster another child lost it

outcome.text: The quartermaster finds your false account beside the harness. Your household loses standing with the stores.

before.title: THE EMPTY TUTOR’S PURSE
before.text: {{guardian}} must meet a tutor’s fee and a tenant’s request for seed. {{contact}} has the household accounts.

choices.label: Read the accounts before asking for more

outcome.text: The accounts show what can be spent on tutors after seed is reserved. Your guardian trusts you with the next petition.

choices.label: Hide the tenant’s petition

outcome.text: The hidden petition is found. The tenants blame your household for a refusal it never openly made.

after.title: THE EMPTY TUTOR’S PURSE
after.text: {{guardian.intro}} has a tutor’s fee to pay and a tenant asking for seed. {{contact}} spreads out the household figures. Both requests are larger than the spare coins.

choices.label: Read the accounts before asking for more

outcome.text: The accounts show what can be spent on tutors after seed is reserved. Your guardian trusts you with the next petition.

choices.label: Hide the tenant’s petition

outcome.text: The hidden petition is found. The tenants blame your household for a refusal it never openly made.

before.title: THE TWO NURSERY SEALS
before.text: {{guardian}} finds rival nursery orders signed by different palace factions. {{contact}} asks which order you carried.

choices.label: Show both seals to the guardian

outcome.text: Both nursery seals reach the guardian. Conflicting orders are corrected before the guards choose sides.

choices.label: Tell each faction the other threatened you

outcome.text: The two palace factions compare your stories. Both now have grounds to distrust your household’s word.

after.title: THE TWO NURSERY SEALS
after.text: {{guardian.intro}} finds two nursery orders from rival palace factions. {{contact}} asks which one you carried. One orders a door locked; the other has already sent someone to open it.

choices.label: Show both seals to the guardian

outcome.text: Both nursery seals reach the guardian. Conflicting orders are corrected before the guards choose sides.

choices.label: Tell each faction the other threatened you

outcome.text: The two palace factions compare your stories. Both now have grounds to distrust your household’s word.

before.title: THE WANDERING MONK
before.text: The travelling monk asks the children to copy “Do not waste parchment.” He has written it on a fresh sheet so large that even the back row can see the irony.

choices.label: Learn the letters, including the expensive ones

outcome.text: You learn enough letters to read the warning yourself. The monk lets you keep a scrap and looks away while you practise.

choices.label: Spend the lesson with Sir Quackbeard

outcome.text: The goose offers no instruction and requires no parchment. You enjoy the company, though the writing remains unread.

choices.label: Introduce the frog to the lesson

outcome.text: The frog leaves a wet impression on the page. You gain a reputation for mischief and the monk gains a very brief pupil with excellent jumping prospects.

after.title: A VERY LARGE WARNING
after.text: {{teacher.intro}} writes “Do not waste parchment” across an enormous clean sheet. Somebody at the back asks whether the warning applies to teachers.

choices.label: Learn to read the warning yourself

outcome.text: You can read the words without help by the end. {{teacher}} lets you keep a scrap, and you fill every corner with letters.

choices.label: Spend the lesson with Sir Quackbeard

outcome.text: Sir Quackbeard settles beside you and goes to sleep. You enjoy the company, but the letters on the sheet remain a mystery.

choices.label: Follow the frog outside

outcome.text: The frog leaps into the ditch and you leap after it. {{teacher}} has an empty place at the bench and a very muddy pupil to look for.

before.title: A MOUNTAIN OF TURNIPS
before.text: {{father}} points out the rows waiting to be weeded. “You can see the end,” {{father}} says, omitting that the end is also where tomorrow begins.

choices.label: Work through the rows with your father

outcome.text: You finish tired and gain your father’s affection. The last row earns a quiet nod that nobody else would recognise as a celebration.

choices.label: Do enough, then hide in the hay

outcome.text: The nap is excellent. Your father’s disappointment is less restful and follows you indoors.

after.title: A MOUNTAIN OF TURNIPS
after.text: {{father.intro}} points to the turnip rows. “You can see the end.” You can, but it appears to be getting farther away whenever you bend down.

choices.label: Weed the rows together

outcome.text: Your hands ache by the last row. {{father}} gives you a quiet nod and takes the heavier basket home.

choices.label: Sneak away to play

outcome.text: You return rested and find {{father}} finishing the rows alone. The spare basket is placed beside you without a word.

before.title: THE MILLER’S BIG SON
before.text: {{other}} collects lunches on behalf of the miller’s big son. The supposed protection consists of not being bothered by the people collecting it.

choices.label: Refuse the protection fee

success.text: You refuse to surrender lunch. {{other}} backs down and remembers exactly who made the collection difficult.

failure.text: You are knocked into the ditch. {{other}} keeps the food and acquires a rival who will remember more than the price of lunch.

choices.label: Surrender the lunch and keep the afternoon quiet

outcome.text: You hand over the food. {{other}} gains confidence in the arrangement and loses some of your trust.

choices.label: Call Sir Quackbeard between you

outcome.text: The goose drives {{other}} back by refusing to negotiate about ankles. The collection stops here, and the collector becomes a named rival.

after.title: THE MILLER’S BIG SON
after.text: {{other.intro}} holds out a hand for your lunch. The miller’s big son supposedly sent them. You have never seen the big son do any of the collecting.

choices.label: Keep your lunch and stand your ground

success.text: {{other}} gives way in front of the other children. You eat your lunch while they stare at you, plainly saving the insult for later.

failure.text: {{other}} shoves you into the ditch and takes the food. You climb out with a scraped knee and a very good memory.

choices.label: Hand it over and get away

outcome.text: {{other}} eats while you watch. You leave before the grin gets any wider.

choices.label: Let Sir Quackbeard handle the ankles

outcome.text: Sir Quackbeard drives {{other}} backward with a hiss. You keep your lunch, and the collector points at you as though you personally sharpened the beak.

before.title: THE SMITH’S CHILD
before.text: Another child keeps finding reasons to pass your fence. Today the reason is a pebble that has been kicked in the same small circle for most of the morning.

choices.label: Offer half your turnip

outcome.text: You split your turnip and gained a friend for life. The finest trade you will ever make.

choices.label: Challenge them to a pebble contest

success.text: You lost the contest on purpose (mostly) and won a friend. Cunning diplomacy.

failure.text: You won too hard and gloated too long. They stomped off. The pebble remains your only trophy.

choices.label: Hide behind the goose

outcome.text: Sir Quackbeard hissed. The smith’s child fled. Your social circle remains: one goose.

after.title: THE CHILD AT YOUR FENCE
after.text: A child keeps stopping outside your fence. Today they kick the same pebble in a circle until you look over. Then they kick it straight to you.

choices.label: Share your turnip

outcome.text: You split the turnip and sit together on the fence. By the time the last piece is gone, you have a new friend.

choices.label: Challenge them to a pebble contest

success.text: You lose by a suspiciously small amount. Your new friend demands a rematch before you have even picked up the pebbles.

failure.text: You win, then explain exactly how much you won by. The other child stalks away and leaves you to admire the pebble alone.

choices.label: Hide behind Sir Quackbeard

outcome.text: Sir Quackbeard hisses the child back down the lane. You are left with one goose and a pebble that nobody wants to kick.

before.title: THE RENT NOTCH
before.text: Your guardian’s tally stick has one notch too many. The bailiff has brought a sack large enough to contain your supper.

choices.label: Compare both halves

outcome.text: The split tally proves the payment. Your household keeps its grain.

choices.label: Cut away the notch

outcome.text: The fresh cut betrays you. Your fellow learner is accused of lending the knife.

choices.label: Ask the bailiff to produce his half

outcome.text: Your guardian brings both halves of the tally to the reeve. Neither can be altered without leaving a scar.

after.title: THE RENT NOTCH
after.text: The bailiff counts an extra rent notch on the household tally. {{classmate}} is holding the grain sack open. If the bailiff is right, there will be very little left for supper.

choices.label: Fit the two halves of the tally together

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks your count and {{classmate}} helps fit the halves. The old notches line up; the extra demand does not.

choices.label: Trim the notch and blame the knife on {{classmate}}

outcome.text: The fresh cut is pale against the old wood. {{mentor}} sees it at once, and {{classmate}} refuses to lend you anything sharp again.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the tally

outcome.text: {{mentor}} runs a thumb along the fresh mark and shows you where to compare it. You finish the count without sacrificing supper.

before.title: THE SEED POT
before.text: A rat has drowned in the pot of seed grain. Your cousin proposes burying the evidence in tomorrow’s bread.

choices.label: Sort the seed together

outcome.text: You save enough clean seed for a strip of field and share the credit.

choices.label: Blame your fellow learner

outcome.text: They are made to scrub the pot. They memorise your smile.

choices.label: Ask how seed should be stored

outcome.text: Your guardian shows you a dry bin with a stone lid. The lesson costs a pot, not a harvest.

after.title: THE SEED POT
after.text: There is a drowned rat in the seed pot. {{classmate}} looks from the rat to the bread dough and says, “We need not mention it.”

choices.label: Help {{classmate}} sort out clean seed

outcome.text: You spread the grain to dry. {{mentor}} checks it with you, and {{classmate}} starts counting what can still be sown.

choices.label: Say {{classmate}} put the rat there

outcome.text: {{classmate}} gets a filthy pot to scrub. {{mentor}} catches your smirk before you can wipe it away.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} how to store the seed

outcome.text: {{mentor}} finds a dry bin with a stone lid. {{classmate}} carries the saved grain while you clean out the old pot.

before.title: LETTERS ON THE DOOR
before.text: Your guardian teaches letters on a soot-blackened door. A neighbour mistakes the alphabet for a curse.

choices.label: Read it aloud

outcome.text: The neighbour apologises to the letter B. Your guardian lets you keep the chalk.

choices.label: Say your classmate wrote it

outcome.text: The neighbour crosses himself at your classmate. Friendship grows colder.

choices.label: Ask your guardian to explain the letters

outcome.text: Your guardian reads a household name aloud. The neighbour recognises it and puts down the holy water.

after.title: LETTERS ON THE DOOR
after.text: {{mentor}} chalks letters onto a soot-blackened door. A neighbour sees the crooked marks and fetches holy water. {{classmate}} helpfully draws a little tail on the B.

choices.label: Read the letters before the bucket arrives

outcome.text: You sound out the words while {{classmate}} rubs off the tail. The neighbour lowers the bucket; {{mentor}} gives you a harder word.

choices.label: Tell the neighbour {{classmate}} wrote the curse

outcome.text: The neighbour makes the sign of the cross at {{classmate}}. {{mentor}} has just watched you write the letters, so the excuse lasts one breath.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to read with you

outcome.text: {{mentor}} guides your finger along a familiar household name. The neighbour recognises it and takes the holy water home.

before.title: THE WOOL ACCOUNT
before.text: The household owes six fleeces. A damp fleece weighs twice as much and smells like a drowned sheep.

choices.label: Dry and count them

outcome.text: The account balances before anyone reaches for a cudgel.

choices.label: Hide the damp one in a rival’s sack

outcome.text: The smell follows your rival into chapel. So does a grievance.

choices.label: Ask the wool buyer for a dry weight

outcome.text: The buyer provides a dry standard. Your guardian teaches you to record it before accepting a fleece.

after.title: THE WOOL ACCOUNT
after.text: You and {{classmate}} must count six fleeces for a buyer. One is dripping onto the floor. {{mentor}} asks whether water has become as valuable as wool.

choices.label: Dry them and work out the true weight

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps spread the wool. {{mentor}} checks the dry weight and lets you finish the count together.

choices.label: Hide the wet fleece in {{classmate}}’s sack

outcome.text: The sack drips all the way to {{mentor}}’s feet. {{classmate}} opens it and looks straight at you.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} for a dry sample to compare

outcome.text: You weigh the sample, then the suspect fleece. {{mentor}} helps you calculate the difference before the buyer comes back.

before.title: THE SAINT WITH TWO ELBOWS
before.text: Your teacher asks you to copy the relic inventory. Saint Aelfric now possesses three elbows and no head.

choices.label: Check the older inventory

outcome.text: You restore one elbow to its rightful saint. Your teacher praises your care.

choices.label: Let your classmate copy the error

outcome.text: The visiting canon questions your classmate before the whole parish.

choices.label: Ask the canon to inspect the relic roll

outcome.text: The canon compares the old roll with yours. Saint Aelfric loses an elbow without further injury.

after.title: THE SAINT WITH TWO ELBOWS
after.text: {{mentor}} sets you to copy the relic list. You give Saint Aelfric three elbows. {{classmate}} peers over and asks whether he used all of them for praying.

choices.label: Check the older list together

outcome.text: {{classmate}} finds the missing saint. {{mentor}} watches you move one elbow to its proper owner and praises the correction.

choices.label: Let {{classmate}} copy your splendid extra elbow

outcome.text: The visiting canon counts the elbows aloud. {{classmate}} recognises your mistake on their own page, and {{mentor}} recognises who lent it.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the relic list

outcome.text: {{mentor}} lays the old list beside yours. You correct the extra elbow without making the saint lose anything else.

before.title: THE PSALTER PIG
before.text: A pig eats the lower half of a psalter page. Your mentor suggests that Providence has abbreviated the lesson.

choices.label: Reconstruct the passage

outcome.text: You and your classmate remember enough to rescue the psalm.

choices.label: Accuse your classmate of feeding it

outcome.text: The pig escapes punishment. Your classmate does not.

choices.label: Bring the damaged page to the priest

outcome.text: The priest borrows a second psalter. You learn how a missing passage is checked rather than invented.

after.title: THE PSALTER PIG
after.text: A pig eats the bottom half of a psalter page. {{classmate}} catches it by one hind leg; {{mentor}} catches the book. Neither rescue restores the words.

choices.label: Rebuild the missing lines with {{classmate}}

outcome.text: Between you, enough of the psalm comes back. {{mentor}} checks a second book and helps you fill the gap honestly.

choices.label: Accuse {{classmate}} of feeding the page to the pig

outcome.text: {{classmate}} lets go of the leg in shock. The pig escapes, and {{mentor}} has seen enough to doubt your story.

choices.label: Bring the torn book to {{mentor}}

outcome.text: {{mentor}} borrows another psalter. You compare the lines while {{classmate}} keeps the pig outside.

before.title: THE BURIAL FEE
before.text: A widow’s husband appears twice in the burial ledger. She refuses to pay for the second funeral on sound theological grounds.

choices.label: Correct the account

outcome.text: The widow keeps her pennies. Your teacher trusts you with the ledger.

choices.label: Copy your rival’s signature beneath it

outcome.text: The widow curses your rival by name. They learn why at vespers.

choices.label: Ask the priest to cancel the duplicate burial

outcome.text: Your teacher strikes the second entry and explains why a clean correction beats a clever excuse.

after.title: THE BURIAL FEE
after.text: A widow finds her husband entered twice in the burial book. “He was difficult,” she tells {{mentor}}, “but I only buried him once.” {{classmate}} is trying not to laugh.

choices.label: Find and correct the duplicate entry

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps find the earlier burial. {{mentor}} checks your correction and the widow keeps her pennies.

choices.label: Put {{classmate}}’s signature under the extra charge

outcome.text: The widow curses {{classmate}} by name. {{mentor}} spots the copied hand, and your classmate learns exactly why everyone is staring.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to strike out the second burial

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks both dates with you and crosses out the duplicate. You take the corrected book back to the widow.

before.title: THE BELL ROPE EXAMINATION
before.text: Your classmate is suspended from the bell rope, clutching the only clean lesson sheet.

choices.label: Help them down and share it

outcome.text: You both pass, though the bell announces it to three parishes.

choices.label: Read the answers while they dangle

outcome.text: Your work is excellent. Your classmate’s opinion of you is precise.

choices.label: Fetch the teacher and a ladder

outcome.text: The teacher lowers your classmate safely. The lesson resumes beneath a very quiet bell.

after.title: THE BELL ROPE EXAMINATION
after.text: {{classmate}} hangs from the bell rope with the only clean lesson sheet clamped between their teeth. Every attempt to speak rings the bell again. {{mentor}} is coming to find out why.

choices.label: Help them down and share the sheet

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks the answers with both of you. The bell rings once more when {{classmate}} finally lets go.

choices.label: Read the answers while {{classmate}} dangles

outcome.text: You finish first. {{mentor}} looks from your neat page to {{classmate}}’s white knuckles and stops looking pleased.

choices.label: Fetch {{mentor}} and something to stand on

outcome.text: {{mentor}} steadies a stool while you guide {{classmate}} down. The lesson resumes with the bell rope tied out of reach.

before.title: THE MASTER’S PERFECT HORSESHOE
before.text: Your master offers the inspector a horseshoe you saw crack beneath the hammer. Your fellow apprentice has been ordered to carry it.

choices.label: Repair it quietly

outcome.text: Your repair holds. The master’s reputation now rests on your hands.

choices.label: Blame the other apprentice

outcome.text: The master docks their supper. They keep the cracked shoe as evidence.

choices.label: Show the crack to the inspector
