outcome.text: The inspector refuses the shoe. Your master accepts the rebuke rather less gracefully than the inspection fee.

after.title: THE MASTER’S PERFECT HORSESHOE
after.text: {{mentor}} selects a horseshoe for inspection. You saw it crack under the hammer. {{classmate}} is about to carry it in on a cushion, which will not improve the metal.

choices.label: Repair the crack with {{classmate}}

outcome.text: {{mentor}} watches your careful repair. {{classmate}} carries in a sound shoe and makes sure your help is mentioned.

choices.label: Blame {{classmate}} for cracking the shoe

outcome.text: {{classmate}} gets the blame before the inspector. {{mentor}} remembers who was at the anvil and asks you to stay behind.

choices.label: Show {{mentor}} the crack before the inspection

outcome.text: {{mentor}} turns the shoe in the light and puts it aside. You help make a sound replacement instead of learning how to hide a split.

before.title: THE STOLEN GUILD SEAL
before.text: A customer wants the guild seal on pewter spoons. The master’s silver sample is locked away with his drinking money.

choices.label: Demand a proper assay

outcome.text: The spoons fail the assay. Your careful work earns the inspector’s attention.

choices.label: Stamp the rival’s mark instead

outcome.text: A false mark reaches the guild court. Your rival begins collecting witnesses.

choices.label: Ask the master to order a public assay

outcome.text: Your master orders the assay in front of witnesses. You learn how a mark binds the maker to the metal.

after.title: THE STOLEN GUILD SEAL
after.text: A customer wants a silver mark stamped on pewter spoons. {{mentor}} sets the proper sample on the bench. {{classmate}} is watching the customer’s purse rather closely.

choices.label: Test the spoons against the real sample

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps with the test. The metal fails; {{mentor}} gives you credit for catching it before the spoons leave.

choices.label: Stamp {{classmate}}’s mark on the false spoons

outcome.text: {{classmate}} is called to explain the mark. {{mentor}} finds the spoons on your side of the bench, still warm from your work.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to test one in front of the customer

outcome.text: {{mentor}} makes you compare the two metals. The customer takes back the purse when the difference can no longer be talked away.

before.title: THE APPRENTICE’S FINGER
before.text: A younger apprentice traps a finger in the vice. The commission is due before the bells.

choices.label: Stop work and free them

outcome.text: The apprentice keeps the finger and helps finish your commission.

choices.label: Tell the master your rival tightened it

outcome.text: The vice is opened. Your rival’s prospects close a little.

choices.label: Call the master to open the vice

outcome.text: The master stops the job and releases the apprentice. You lose an hour and learn why a commission has no fingers.

after.title: THE APPRENTICE’S FINGER
after.text: {{classmate}} traps a finger in the vice. The job is already late. {{mentor}} calls from the next room, asking why the hammering has stopped.

choices.label: Free the finger and finish together

outcome.text: {{mentor}} helps check the hand. {{classmate}} works beside you once the pain settles, and you learn how to handle the vice safely.

choices.label: Tell {{mentor}} that {{classmate}} jammed it on purpose

outcome.text: {{mentor}} frees the hand, then hears your excuse. {{classmate}} holds the swollen finger against their chest and will not look at you.

choices.label: Call {{mentor}} before you turn the screw

outcome.text: {{mentor}} steadies the trapped hand while you ease the vice open. The job can wait; the finger cannot.

before.title: THE MASTERPIECE IN THE ASHES
before.text: A spark lands on your measured drawing. Your rival’s drawing is excellent, and unattended.

choices.label: Rebuild the measurements

outcome.text: Your teacher tests every line. The work is slow and yours.

choices.label: Present the rival’s drawing

outcome.text: The compass holes match their old work. Your mentor is less foolish than you hoped.

choices.label: Ask the master to check your surviving measurements

outcome.text: The master helps reconstruct the burnt drawing. Each borrowed measurement is acknowledged in the margin.

after.title: THE MASTERPIECE IN THE ASHES
after.text: A spark burns through your measured drawing. {{classmate}}’s neat copy lies unattended beside it. {{mentor}} will want both pieces of work before supper.

choices.label: Ask {{classmate}} to help rebuild the measurements

outcome.text: {{classmate}} shares the figures while you redraw the lost lines. {{mentor}} checks the finished work and credits you both.

choices.label: Hand in {{classmate}}’s drawing as your own

outcome.text: {{mentor}} recognises the compass holes from the earlier work. {{classmate}} holds out a hand for the drawing and leaves it there until you give it back.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the surviving lines

outcome.text: {{mentor}} helps you recover the measurements from the unburnt corner. The new drawing is slower to make, but it is yours.

before.title: THE DEVIL IN THE MARGIN
before.text: Your classmate draws a bishop being swallowed by a snail. The dean calls for the artist.

choices.label: Defend it as a moral warning

outcome.text: The dean accepts a sermon on vanity. Your classmate owes you a kindness.

choices.label: Name your rival instead

outcome.text: Your rival scrapes parchment for a week and starts a private list of sins.

choices.label: Ask the dean what the snail signifies

outcome.text: The dean invents an allegory with astonishing speed. Your mentor explains which parts can safely be repeated.

after.title: THE DEVIL IN THE MARGIN
after.text: {{classmate}} draws a bishop being swallowed by a snail. {{mentor}} finds the picture while the ink is wet. The snail is wearing a remarkably familiar mitre.

choices.label: Defend the picture as a warning against vanity

outcome.text: {{mentor}} makes you explain the warning. {{classmate}} keeps a straight face, then whispers thanks when the page is put away.

choices.label: Say {{classmate}} drew it to mock the bishop

outcome.text: {{classmate}} has to scrape the picture off the parchment. {{mentor}} notices that your explanation changes once the scraping starts.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} what the snail could mean

outcome.text: {{mentor}} finds a solemn explanation with surprising speed. You learn which parts of it are safe to repeat outside the room.

before.title: THE GREEK THAT WASN’T
before.text: Your mentor’s prized Greek quotation is a laundry account in a merchant’s cipher.

choices.label: Translate it privately

outcome.text: The master changes his lecture. You receive access to a better manuscript.

choices.label: Let your rival recite it

outcome.text: The chapter learns the price of washing six shirts. Your rival learns betrayal.

choices.label: Show the quotation to your teacher in private

outcome.text: Your teacher replaces the quotation before the lecture. You receive a lesson in translating before pontificating.

after.title: THE GREEK THAT WASN’T
after.text: {{mentor}} proudly reads a Greek quotation. {{classmate}} turns it the right way up: it is a merchant’s laundry list, with a great deal to say about stained shirts.

choices.label: Translate it quietly before the lecture

outcome.text: You and {{classmate}} work through the list. {{mentor}} changes the quotation and gives you a better passage to study.

choices.label: Encourage {{classmate}} to recite it to the chapter

outcome.text: The chapter hears the price of washing six shirts. {{mentor}} sees your face, and {{classmate}} realises why you were so eager to help.

choices.label: Show {{mentor}} the list in private

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks your translation and shuts the book. The lecture begins with a different quotation.

before.title: THE FASTING DISPUTATION
before.text: The chapter argues whether a goose is a fish while the cook holds the knife.

choices.label: Argue from the text

outcome.text: Your argument saves the goose until supper. Your teacher respects the scholarship.

choices.label: Attribute the heresy to your rival

outcome.text: Your rival must defend a goose they have never met.

choices.label: Ask the cook to suspend judgement

outcome.text: The cook postpones the knife while your mentor checks the authorities. Theology briefly becomes useful to a goose.

after.title: THE FASTING DISPUTATION
after.text: The chapter is arguing over whether a goose counts as fish on a fast day. {{mentor}} wants your argument. {{classmate}} is guarding the goose from a cook who seems ready to settle it.

choices.label: Check the text with {{classmate}}

outcome.text: {{mentor}} hears a careful argument instead of a hungry guess. {{classmate}} gets the goose out of the kitchen while the discussion continues.

choices.label: Blame {{classmate}} for the forbidden supper

outcome.text: The chapter turns on {{classmate}}. {{mentor}} has heard you arguing for the meal and makes you answer for your own words.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to keep the cook waiting

outcome.text: {{mentor}} makes you find the relevant passage before anyone picks up a knife. The goose gets a little longer to be a goose.

before.title: THE MEDICAL GLOSS
before.text: A manuscript recommends bloodletting after a faint. Your classmate has fainted directly beneath it.

choices.label: Compare the herbal commentary

outcome.text: You keep the lancet shut and fetch water. Your classmate recovers.

choices.label: Forge the rival’s endorsement

outcome.text: The mentor catches the forged hand before the lancet opens. The grudge remains real.

choices.label: Fetch the infirmarer before the lancet

outcome.text: The infirmarer orders water and rest. Your teacher makes you record the observation beside the disputed gloss.

after.title: THE MEDICAL GLOSS
after.text: A manuscript recommends bleeding anyone who faints. {{classmate}} has fainted over it. {{mentor}} reaches the desk while somebody is looking for a lancet.

choices.label: Read the patient before trusting the page

outcome.text: You help {{classmate}} lie safely while {{mentor}} checks their breathing. You compare what happened with what the manuscript actually claims.

choices.label: Say {{classmate}} demanded the lancet

outcome.text: {{mentor}} puts down the lancet and asks who suggested it. {{classmate}} hears you shift the blame and remembers it once the room stops spinning.

choices.label: Fetch {{mentor}} before anyone uses the blade

outcome.text: {{mentor}} arranges immediate care. Later, you set the actual symptoms beside the old advice and mark the dangerous difference.

before.title: THE PAGE AND THE PRIVY
before.text: Your first watch is outside the lord’s privy. A visitor insists the password is a matter of terrible urgency.

choices.label: Fetch the watch sergeant

outcome.text: The visitor is admitted under escort. The sergeant trusts your judgement.

choices.label: Send your rival to stop him

outcome.text: Your rival receives the chamber pot and the blame.

choices.label: Ask the sergeant to take the watch

outcome.text: The sergeant handles the visitor and explains when urgency is an excuse and when it is a medical fact.

after.title: THE PAGE AND THE PRIVY
after.text: Your watch is outside the lord’s privy. {{classmate}} has a desperate visitor by the elbow, and {{mentor}} has told you not to let anyone through.

choices.label: Hear the visitor before enforcing the order

outcome.text: You and {{classmate}} find a sensible way to help without abandoning the watch. {{mentor}} hears a clear account rather than a wet complaint.

choices.label: Send the visitor to {{classmate}}’s post instead

outcome.text: The complaint lands on {{classmate}}. {{mentor}} follows the visitor’s route back to you, while your classmate begins taking a careful interest in your next watch.

choices.label: Fetch {{mentor}} to settle the urgent problem

outcome.text: {{mentor}} handles the visitor and shows you how to keep the watch without making misery its main purpose.

before.title: THE SQUIRE’S WOODEN HORSE
before.text: Your classmate’s practice saddle slips. The master calls this an opportunity to demonstrate courage.

choices.label: Secure the girth first

outcome.text: Your classmate lands upright and later returns the favour.

choices.label: Loosen the rival’s girth

outcome.text: The fall is noticed. So are your hands on the buckle.

choices.label: Ask the riding master to inspect the saddle

outcome.text: The master repairs the girth. You are made to inspect every buckle before the next ride.

after.title: THE SQUIRE’S WOODEN HORSE
after.text: {{classmate}}’s practice saddle slips beneath the rider. {{mentor}} calls it a lesson in balance. The horse appears to be learning how far a pupil can slide.

choices.label: Check the girth and help remount

outcome.text: {{classmate}} holds the horse while you fix the girth. {{mentor}} checks it and lets you practise together on sound tack.

choices.label: Claim {{classmate}} loosened your saddle

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks the straps and finds your careless fastening. {{classmate}} hears the accusation before you can take it back.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to inspect the tack

outcome.text: {{mentor}} makes you check every buckle before the next ride. {{classmate}} holds the reins and waits until you get it right.

before.title: THE BLUNT LANCE
before.text: The training lance bears a fresh split. The armourer offers to paint over it before the inspection.

choices.label: Replace the shaft

outcome.text: You lose an afternoon and save a face. Your master credits the inspection.

choices.label: Put it in your rival’s rack

outcome.text: The shaft breaks in their hands. They remember who visited the rack.

choices.label: Bring the shaft to the armourer

outcome.text: The armourer replaces the split wood and teaches you where a painted crack will still show under pressure.

after.title: THE BLUNT LANCE
after.text: A fresh split runs down the training lance. {{mentor}} wants it ready for drill. {{classmate}} holds up a pot of paint and raises an eyebrow.

choices.label: Replace the damaged shaft together

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps fit sound wood. {{mentor}} checks the lance, then gives you both another turn at the drill.

choices.label: Give the painted split lance to {{classmate}}

outcome.text: The paint flakes when {{mentor}} tests the shaft. {{classmate}} sees the split and realises why you insisted on swapping.

choices.label: Bring the shaft to {{mentor}} before drill

outcome.text: {{mentor}} finds a sound replacement and shows you where a painted crack will still give under pressure.

before.title: THE HUNGRY MUSTER
before.text: The muster roll includes four dead soldiers and a horse listed as a cousin.

choices.label: Recount the living

outcome.text: Rations reach the actual company. Your teacher praises useful arithmetic.

choices.label: Sign your rival’s name to it

outcome.text: Your rival answers to the captain for a horse’s family tree.

choices.label: Ask the quartermaster to recount the roll

outcome.text: The quartermaster removes four ghosts and one horse. Your tutor makes you copy the corrected ration order.

after.title: THE HUNGRY MUSTER
after.text: {{mentor}} asks you to check the muster. There are four dead soldiers on it and a horse drawing a cook’s wage. {{classmate}} wants to meet this very talented horse.

choices.label: Recount the living soldiers with {{classmate}}

outcome.text: You cross-check the names together. {{mentor}} approves the corrected roll and has a useful drill ready for you.

choices.label: Put {{classmate}}’s name beside the extra rations

outcome.text: {{classmate}} is called to account for food never received. {{mentor}} compares the marks with your earlier work and calls you over.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the suspicious names

outcome.text: {{mentor}} removes the false entries while you copy the corrected ration order. The horse returns to being paid in oats.

before.title: THE WRONG COAT OF ARMS
before.text: Your tutor asks you to seat two cousins whose fathers died fighting over the same painted badger.

choices.label: Check the genealogy

outcome.text: You separate the cousins by three bishops. Dinner survives.

choices.label: Give your rival the seating plan

outcome.text: They face two angry households. Your tutor identifies the handwriting.

choices.label: Ask the herald to verify the disputed arms

outcome.text: The herald seats both cousins far from sharp cutlery. Your tutor explains the disputed descent.

after.title: THE WRONG COAT OF ARMS
after.text: {{mentor}} asks you to seat two hostile cousins at supper. {{classmate}} has drawn crossed swords between their names on the plan.

choices.label: Check the family ties before placing them

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps redraw the table. {{mentor}} approves seats with several calm people and a great deal of food between the cousins.

choices.label: Put {{classmate}}’s name on the insulting plan

outcome.text: The cousins demand to know why {{classmate}} put them together. {{mentor}} has already seen your first drawing and asks for it back.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the disputed arms

outcome.text: {{mentor}} helps you trace the descent, then moves the cousins away from the sharp cutlery. You keep the corrected plan.

before.title: THE ACCOUNT OF THE SWANS
before.text: The steward counts twelve swans. The kitchen accounts for thirteen swan pies.

choices.label: Trace the kitchen purchases

outcome.text: The thirteenth bird was a goose. Your tutor commends the audit.

choices.label: Charge the missing bird to your rival

outcome.text: The steward demands payment. Your rival begins auditing you.

choices.label: Ask the steward to reconcile the kitchen roll

outcome.text: The steward finds the goose receipt. You learn to audit the purchases before accusing the cook.

after.title: THE ACCOUNT OF THE SWANS
after.text: The kitchen has paid for thirteen swans and received twelve. {{mentor}} gives you the receipts. {{classmate}} points out that the thirteenth looks suspiciously like a goose.

choices.label: Find the goose receipt together

outcome.text: {{classmate}} tracks down the cheaper bird. {{mentor}} praises the careful sum before anyone accuses the cook of eating a swan.

choices.label: Slip the missing swan into {{classmate}}’s account

outcome.text: {{mentor}} finds two different hands in the account. {{classmate}} has to explain a purchase you made up for them.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to compare the kitchen receipts

outcome.text: {{mentor}} puts the goose receipt beside the swan price. You correct the total and return the money to the proper column.

before.title: THE EMBASSY’S CHAIRS
before.text: An envoy’s chair is an inch lower than yours. His secretary calls it an insult to the whole coast.

choices.label: Offer equal stools

outcome.text: Everyone suffers equally. Your tutor calls this diplomacy.

choices.label: Say your rival ordered the chairs

outcome.text: The envoy records your rival’s name beside the word grievance.

choices.label: Ask the chamberlain to change every seat

outcome.text: The chamberlain replaces the chairs. Your tutor notes that equal discomfort is a workable diplomatic settlement.

after.title: THE EMBASSY’S CHAIRS
after.text: An envoy’s chair is an inch lower than yours. {{classmate}} notices first; {{mentor}} arrives just as the envoy’s secretary demands a ruler.

choices.label: Change the seating without singling anyone out

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps swap the chairs. {{mentor}} watches the envoy sit down without having to defend anyone’s knees.

choices.label: Tell the envoy {{classmate}} chose the low chair

outcome.text: {{classmate}} receives a frosty bow. {{mentor}} has watched you move the chairs and is unimpressed by the explanation.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to replace the whole row

outcome.text: Every guest gets an equally uncomfortable chair. {{mentor}} lets you explain the seating plan while nobody can claim a shorter seat.

before.title: THE TENANT’S PETITION
before.text: A tenant petitions for seed. Your tutor says this is an exercise in household administration. The tenant says he is an exercise in starvation.

choices.label: Check the granary and draft relief

outcome.text: The lesson becomes a workable petition. Your classmate helps calculate it.

choices.label: Forge your rival’s refusal

outcome.text: The tenant curses your rival. Your tutor catches the borrowed seal.

choices.label: Ask the tutor to examine the seed petition

outcome.text: Your tutor measures the household’s need against the stores. The petitioner receives an answer based on grain rather than manners.

after.title: THE TENANT’S PETITION
after.text: A tenant asks for seed grain. {{mentor}} calls it a lesson in managing a household. “Mine is hungry,” the tenant replies. {{classmate}} stops fiddling with the seal.

choices.label: Count what can safely be spared

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps work out the grain. {{mentor}} checks your proposal and approves an answer the household can actually carry out.

choices.label: Forge a refusal under {{classmate}}’s name

outcome.text: The tenant blames {{classmate}}. {{mentor}} catches the copied seal and makes you read the refusal aloud to the person it would hurt.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the stores with you

outcome.text: You count the grain beside {{mentor}} instead of guessing from the tenant’s manners. The request gets a practical answer.

before.title: THE WINTER ACCOUNT
before.text: {{mentor}} brings your household ledger. Winter grain and a creditor fall due together.

choices.label: Plan the stores with {{classmate}}

outcome.text: The plan protects seed and supper.

choices.label: Hide the arrears in the seed account

outcome.text: Your colleague finds the missing debt beside their signature.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to review the winter stores

outcome.text: Your tutor separates the seed reserve from the debt payment and sets a practical accounting exercise.

after.title: THE WINTER ACCOUNT
after.text: The grain reserve and a creditor both need the same coins. {{mentor}} brings the figures; {{classmate}} brings a loaf to make sure the lesson lasts until supper.

choices.label: Plan the stores with {{classmate}}

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks the sums. You and {{classmate}} find enough for seed and supper without making a debt disappear.

choices.label: Hide the arrears under {{classmate}}’s figures

outcome.text: {{classmate}} finds the debt tucked beside their signature. {{mentor}} asks you to add it up again, this time with every number showing.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check what can be spared

outcome.text: {{mentor}} keeps the seed grain separate while you and {{classmate}} work out the payment. You leave with a plan you can explain at home.

before.title: AN EVENING OF LETTERS
before.text: After work, {{classmate}} asks you to read a tenancy clause neither of you understood as children.

choices.label: Read it against the old agreement

outcome.text: Your shared study finds the changed rent.

choices.label: Pretend the clause favours you

outcome.text: Your colleague carries your interpretation to the landlord.

choices.label: Read the disputed tenancy clause with {{mentor}}

outcome.text: Your tutor compares both agreements and asks you to explain each changed obligation.

after.title: AN EVENING OF LETTERS
after.text: After work, {{classmate}} brings a tenancy clause neither of you understood as children. {{mentor}} fetches the older agreement. The rent has grown much faster than the words.

choices.label: Read the two agreements side by side

outcome.text: {{classmate}} finds the changed line while {{mentor}} checks your reading. You can both explain the new rent without guessing.

choices.label: Pretend the clause gives you the advantage

outcome.text: {{classmate}} takes your reading to the landlord and comes back with the old agreement. {{mentor}} does not need to ask which line you left out.

choices.label: Read the disputed sentence with {{mentor}}

outcome.text: You work through the unfamiliar words with {{mentor}}. The altered obligation is much less impressive once you can read all of it.

before.title: THE LATE READER
before.text: {{mentor}} reserves an evening for adults learning their letters. {{classmate}} brings a contract rather than a psalter.

choices.label: Read the contract together

outcome.text: You separate the obligations from the ornament.

choices.label: Copy a fluent reader’s exercise

outcome.text: The copied hand wins praise that belongs to someone else.

choices.label: Ask for an evening reading exercise

outcome.text: Your teacher sets a short contract passage that can be studied after paid work.

after.title: THE LATE READER
after.text: {{classmate}} brings a contract to the evening reading lesson. {{mentor}} starts with the large decorated initial. “That bit owes nothing,” your classmate says. “Try the rest.”

choices.label: Read the contract together

outcome.text: You and {{classmate}} pick out the promises hiding under the fine writing. {{mentor}} checks each one and lets you read the last sentence unaided.

choices.label: Copy {{classmate}}’s fluent exercise

outcome.text: {{mentor}} praises the borrowed page until {{classmate}} lays the original beside it. The two pages have the same ink blot.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} for a shorter passage to start with

outcome.text: {{mentor}} covers the rest of the page. You get through one hard sentence properly before trying the next.

before.title: A LETTER HOME
before.text: {{classmate}} needs a letter to a relative who has left for work. The parish desk is finally quiet.

choices.label: Help compose an honest letter

outcome.text: Your colleague entrusts you with the reply.

choices.label: Read the private lines aloud for a laugh

outcome.text: The laughter travels; so does the betrayal.

choices.label: Ask how to write a private reply

outcome.text: Your teacher helps form a respectful letter while preserving your colleague’s confidence.

after.title: A LETTER HOME
after.text: {{classmate}} needs a letter for a relative working away from home. The first attempt contains a great deal of weather and none of what they want to say. {{mentor}} leaves you a quiet corner.

choices.label: Help write what they actually mean

outcome.text: {{classmate}} reads it back slowly and folds it with care. {{mentor}} checks the difficult words without prying into the rest.

choices.label: Read the private lines aloud for a laugh

outcome.text: The room laughs before {{classmate}} can take the page away. {{mentor}} sends the listeners back to work; your classmate folds the letter without your help.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} how to keep the letter private

outcome.text: {{mentor}} helps you find plain words for the reply. {{classmate}} watches you leave the private lines covered.

before.title: THE LATE APPRENTICE
before.text: An older apprentice is assigned the heaviest work. {{mentor}} asks whether your previous experience changes the arrangement.

choices.label: Propose a trial piece and fair rotation

outcome.text: Your work earns an adult place at the bench.

choices.label: Claim {{classmate}} made the flawed trial piece

outcome.text: The commission carries an innocent maker’s mark.

choices.label: Ask for an assessment of your previous craft work

outcome.text: Your master tests your existing skills and records what the late apprenticeship still requires.

after.title: THE LATE APPRENTICE
after.text: {{classmate}} gets the heavy lifting because an older apprentice is supposedly stronger. {{mentor}} asks you to choose the work for a trial piece. Your classmate is rubbing a shoulder.

choices.label: Suggest a fair rotation and a proper trial

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps with the piece while you share the lifting. {{mentor}} tests the result and gives both of you useful work.

choices.label: Put {{classmate}}’s mark on your flawed trial piece

outcome.text: {{mentor}} finds the fault. {{classmate}} recognises the piece they helped you carry and sees the mark you added.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to test the work you already know

outcome.text: {{mentor}} gives you a small job at the bench and watches your hands. You find out which parts of the late apprenticeship still need practice.

before.title: THE EVENING MASTERPIECE
before.text: Your paying work leaves one evening to finish the apprenticeship sample. {{classmate}} offers measurements.

choices.label: Credit their help and submit your own work

outcome.text: The master tests the work and acknowledges both hands.

choices.label: Submit their sample under your mark

outcome.text: Your colleague keeps the original drawing.

choices.label: Show {{mentor}} your unfinished masterpiece

outcome.text: The master checks the surviving measurements and sets a smaller, honest trial piece.

after.title: THE EVENING MASTERPIECE
after.text: You have one evening to finish your apprenticeship sample. {{classmate}} offers their measurements. {{mentor}} will test the piece in the morning. The first cock has already crowed.

choices.label: Use the figures and credit their help

outcome.text: {{mentor}} tests the finished piece. You name the help, and {{classmate}} stays to hear the answer beside you.

choices.label: Put your mark on {{classmate}}’s finished sample

outcome.text: {{mentor}} asks about a joint you have never cut. {{classmate}} produces the drawing and waits for you to stop describing it.

choices.label: Show {{mentor}} what you can honestly finish

outcome.text: {{mentor}} sets a smaller trial from the surviving measurements. You have time to make it properly rather than sign somebody else’s work.

before.title: THE INFERMARER’S COMMENTARY
before.text: {{mentor}} asks your adult seminar to compare a fever diary with an old authority. The patient’s actual course contradicts the gloss.

choices.label: Record the observations honestly

outcome.text: The seminar adopts a more careful account of care.

choices.label: Alter the diary to flatter the authority

outcome.text: Your colleague retains the unaltered observations.

choices.label: Compare the fever diary with {{mentor}}

outcome.text: Your teacher asks you to distinguish an observed symptom from an authority’s assumption.

after.title: THE INFERMARER’S COMMENTARY
after.text: {{mentor}} sets a fever diary beside an old commentary. The patient recovered on the day the commentary says recovery was impossible. {{classmate}} asks whether the patient has been told.

choices.label: Compare the observations honestly

outcome.text: {{classmate}} helps set out the dates. {{mentor}} makes you separate what was seen from what the commentary merely assumed.

choices.label: Change the diary to flatter the old authority

outcome.text: {{classmate}} keeps the original notes. When {{mentor}} compares the dates, your corrected patient appears to have recovered twice.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the symptoms with you

outcome.text: You work through the diary beside {{mentor}}, marking the actual symptoms before discussing the old explanation.

before.title: THE VISITING EXAMINER
before.text: A visiting examiner asks how your learning was acquired while you worked. {{mentor}} can certify the hours actually completed.

choices.label: Submit the honest record

outcome.text: Your remaining requirements are written clearly.

choices.label: Borrow a completed clerical certificate

outcome.text: The borrowed certificate passes today. A later review may compare the signatures.

choices.label: Ask for the actual examination requirements

outcome.text: The examiner writes down the hours and arguments still required for a legitimate certificate.

after.title: THE VISITING EXAMINER
after.text: A visiting examiner asks which study you completed between paid jobs. {{mentor}} has the real hours; {{classmate}} has a finished certificate with remarkably tempting blank space.

choices.label: Present your honest study record

outcome.text: {{mentor}} confirms the hours. {{classmate}} helps you list what remains, and the examiner can question you on work you actually did.

choices.label: Borrow the completed clerical certificate

outcome.text: The paper passes the first inspection. {{classmate}} recognises the borrowed certificate, and its signatures may still be checked later.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} for the real examination requirements

outcome.text: {{mentor}} lists the hours and arguments still needed. You practise one of the difficult questions instead of practising a signature.

before.title: THE VETERAN AT DRILL
before.text: {{classmate}} has seen a siege; you are learning formations after years in another trade. {{mentor}} asks for a plan.

choices.label: Combine practical experience with the drill

outcome.text: The exercise gives both adult learners useful work.

choices.label: Claim their campaign experience as yours

outcome.text: The sergeant begins asking which company remembers you.

choices.label: Review the drill with the veteran and {{mentor}}

outcome.text: Your trainer sets an exercise that tests the veteran’s experience and your understanding together.

after.title: THE VETERAN AT DRILL
after.text: {{mentor}} asks for a plan to defend a narrow gate. {{classmate}} draws a wonderful formation with you standing directly in front of every spear.

choices.label: Work through the drill together

outcome.text: You and {{classmate}} move the markers until both lines have cover. {{mentor}} checks the plan and sends you out to try it.

choices.label: Present {{classmate}}’s plan as your own

outcome.text: {{mentor}} asks why your plan has {{classmate}}’s initials in the corner. {{classmate}} waits to hear the answer.

choices.label: Review the drill beside {{mentor}}

outcome.text: {{mentor}} moves you out of the spear line and makes you explain why the new position is safer. You practise until you can hold it.

before.title: THE CONTRACTED WATCH
before.text: Your training company must cover a night watch while keeping time for its adult recruits’ paid work.

choices.label: Draw a fair rotation

outcome.text: The company trusts the rota because you serve it too.

choices.label: Put your colleague on every cold watch

outcome.text: The rota is copied, along with its author’s name.

choices.label: Ask the captain to review the watch rotation

outcome.text: The captain checks the recruits’ paid work and makes you explain a fair allocation of cold watches.

after.title: THE CONTRACTED WATCH
after.text: The adult recruits have paid work in the morning, but somebody must stand the cold watch. {{classmate}} finds their name on nearly every empty space. {{mentor}} hands you the rota.

choices.label: Take your share and make a fair rotation

outcome.text: {{classmate}} checks the new list while {{mentor}} checks your name is on it too. You learn the watch instead of merely assigning it.

choices.label: Leave {{classmate}} on every cold watch

outcome.text: {{classmate}} makes a second copy. {{mentor}} reads it at breakfast while you try to look well rested for an innocent reason.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to review the watch with you

outcome.text: You and {{mentor}} fit the watches around the recruits’ paid work. {{classmate}} keeps a turn, but so do you.

before.title: THE PRIVATE TUTOR’S TABLE
before.text: {{mentor}} teaches court practice to adults. {{classmate}} brings a petition from their own household.

choices.label: Draft advice from the actual accounts

outcome.text: Your tutor commends a useful answer rather than a fine bow.

choices.label: Trade their private grievance for influence

outcome.text: The petition returns to its author with your name attached.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to examine the household petition

outcome.text: The tutor checks the figures and asks you to justify each proposed relief payment.

after.title: THE PRIVATE TUTOR’S TABLE
after.text: {{classmate}} brings a household request to the adult lesson. {{mentor}} asks for useful advice. Your classmate puts away the beautifully phrased version and shows you the unpaid bills.

choices.label: Work from the actual household figures

outcome.text: {{mentor}} checks your proposed relief. {{classmate}} has an answer that may help at home, rather than a compliment to repeat at supper.

choices.label: Trade their private grievance for influence

outcome.text: The story comes back to {{classmate}} with your name attached. {{mentor}} sets aside your polished advice and asks about the confidence you broke.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to check the relief you propose

outcome.text: {{mentor}} counts the grain with you before you promise it. {{classmate}} leaves with a smaller, affordable request.

before.title: THE ADULT AUDIENCE
before.text: An envoy questions why your household can afford tutoring while tenants petition for seed.

choices.label: Explain the accounts and propose affordable relief

outcome.text: Your reasoning survives questions from your colleague.

choices.label: Produce a borrowed court certificate

outcome.text: The document opens a door. The seal may be checked later.

choices.label: Ask for a witnessed court examination

outcome.text: Your tutor offers a legitimate assessment instead of a borrowed seal; the remaining preparation is recorded.

after.title: THE ADULT AUDIENCE
after.text: An envoy asks why the household pays for tutoring while tenants need seed. {{mentor}} gives you the figures; {{classmate}} waits to see whether your answer contains any grain.

choices.label: Explain the figures and offer affordable relief

outcome.text: You answer the difficult questions while {{classmate}} checks the sums. {{mentor}} has you defend a practical decision rather than a borrowed phrase.

choices.label: Produce a borrowed court certificate

outcome.text: The seal opens a door for now. {{classmate}} recognises the document, and a later examination may ask what you actually learned.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} for an honest assessment

outcome.text: {{mentor}} offers a witnessed examination. You work on the questions still beyond you instead of pretending the certificate answered them.
